transcript:
User: Hi — I saw your ad on Facebook about answering missed calls. I keep losing patients after hours, so I'm curious how it works.
Agent: Got it, thanks for sharing that — losing patients after hours is really common. Our system steps in when no one can answer, talks to the caller right away, books the appointment or takes a detailed message, and sends it to you so that “missed call” doesn’t turn into a lost patient.

Before I go deeper into the how, can you tell me what usually happens right now if a patient calls after-hours — does it go to voicemail, an answering service, or just ring out?
User: It goes straight to voicemail after hours, and we get about 20 calls like that each week.
Agent: Mhm, so about 20 after-hours calls a week are just hitting voicemail — and some of those are likely going to another provider instead of waiting. 

When those patients do manage to get through the next day, are they mostly new patients trying to book, or existing patients with urgent issues?
User: Mostly new patients trying to book appointments, and I think around half would schedule if someone answered.
Agent: Right, so you’ve got about 20 after-hours calls a week, mostly new patients, and roughly half of them would actually book if someone just picked up — that adds up quickly. 

Has anyone ever walked you through what that’s really costing you each week, or do you want to do a quick back-of-the-napkin math on it together?
User: I haven't done the math yet, but I'd love to understand what it's costing me. How does it work?
Agent: Makes sense — and yeah, it’s hard to fix what you haven’t seen in numbers yet. 

So ballpark, when one of those new patients does book, what’s the average value of that first visit or treatment for you in dollars?
User: For us, the average appointment value is around $650.
Agent: So with your numbers, it’s roughly $6,500 a week, or about $28,000 a month, walking out the door from those after-hours calls. 

What we do is simple: when your office is closed or busy, our system answers instantly, talks to the patient like a trained staff member, books the appointment or collects all their info, and sends it straight to you so those calls turn into scheduled visits instead of voicemails. 

Since this is already costing you around $28k a month, it’s worth a proper 20‑minute walkthrough — I can show you exactly how it would handle your after‑hours calls and what your numbers look like with it on; would you rather do that later this week or next week?
User: Let's book the live call for tomorrow if available — I'd love to see how it works.
Agent: Love that — we can definitely look at tomorrow. 

First off, what’s your first name?
User: My first name is Maria.
Agent: Got it, Maria, thanks.  

And what’s your last name?
User: My last name is Gonzales.
Agent: Thanks, Maria Gonzales.  

What’s the name of your practice?
Agent: Got it.  

And what’s the name of your practice, Maria?
User: The name of my practice is Bright Smile Dental.
Agent: Perfect, Bright Smile Dental.  

And is the number you’re calling from the best number for us to text your appointment confirmation to?
User: Yes, please use my best contact number, +13125551234, for the appointment confirmation.
Agent: Perfect, we’ll use that Central time number.  

For tomorrow, I can get you in as soon as 10:00 AM or 10:45 AM Central — which works better for you?
User: Let's book the live call for 10:45 AM Central tomorrow.
Agent: One moment while I confirm that on our side.
Agent: Maria, you’re all set for tomorrow at 10:45 AM Central with Jay — we’ll walk through exactly how to stop losing those after-hours patients at Bright Smile Dental. You’ll get a text in a moment with the confirmation and a link to reschedule if you ever need to. Is there anything else you need from me right now?
